attachments.text:
Chapter 6: Board of Directors Meetings


Correspondence

Excepting confidential correspondence, all materials distributed to the Board for discussion or
consideration at a public meeting are public records.

Special Meetings

Special meetings may be called by the President or any three Directors with strict notification
requirements delivered to the public at least 24 hours before the time of the meeting.

The Brown Act provides mariy other restrictions and requirements; this chapter is intended merely as a
summary and overview of the Act.




                                                    Page 24

                            CCWD Board of Directors Procedures Manual - March ~2026

Chapter 1:
Confrlicts & Liability


✓ Generally, public officials are prohibited from having a financial interest in a decision or a
  financial interest in a contract.
✓ Annual economic disclosure statements are required of all Board members (Government
  Code Section 81000 et seq.) that disclose potential economic conflicts of interest.
✓ Board members may not accept gifts from any single source totaling more than $.§.90-630 in
  a calendar year.
✓ Board members must report single source gifts totaling more than $50 in a calendar year.


Conflict of_ Interest
State laws are in place that attempt to eliminate any action by a Board member that may reflect a real
or even perceived conflict of interest. The purpose of such laws and regulations is to ensure that all
actions are taken in the public interest.

If at any time a member believes a potential for conflict of interest exists with respect to any matter,
they are encouraged to consult with CCWD legal counsel or private legal counsel for advice on
proceeding.

There are two primary laws that govern conflicts of interest for public officials in California - the
Political Reform Act and Government Code Section 1090. In general terms, the Political Reform Act
prohibits a public official from having a financial interest in a decision before the official. Section 1090
prohibits a public official from having a financial interest in CCWD contracts.

The Fair Political Practices Commission (FPPC) has published regulations and opinions on conflicts of
interest that are useful in determining whether a particular financial interest or decision could give rise
to disqualification based on a potential conflict of interest.



Disqualification from Participating in Consideration of Board Agenda
Item
Pursuant to amendments to the Government Code enacted in 2002 and regulations adopted by the
FPPC in May 2003, if a Director has a conflict of interest with regard to any agenda item, a specific
process should be followed.




                                                      Page 25

                             CCWD Board of Directors Procedures Manual - March 20262W5

                                   Chapter 7: Board of Directors Meetings


    1. After the agenda item is called, but before discussion or voting, the Director shall publicly state
       that they have a potential conflict of interest as defined by the Political Reform Act and will
       recuse themselves from any discussion and voting on the item. The Director's statement must
       be made part of the minutes. An example of a proper recusal statement follows:

                 "The matter before the Board concerns a property owned by NAME. I am an employee
                 of NAME (or NAME'S company), therefore according to the Political Reform Act, NAME is
                 a source of income to me. As required by the Political Reform Act I will recuse myself
                 from consideration of this item, step away from dais, and will leave the room" until the
                 item is concluded.

    2.   The Director shall specifically identify the type of economic interest giving rise to the conflict
         (e.g., investment, interest in real property, business position, personal financial effect, or
         receipt or promise of income or gifts).

    3.   The Director shall leave the room and they may not be counted toward achieving a quorum for
         the Board's consideration of the item.

    4.   If the conflict is with regard to a closed session matter, prior to the closed session the Director
         shall publicly announce that they have a conflict of interest that requires recusal. The
         announcement shall be included in the minutes and the Director shall not attend the closed
         session or be provided information or m~terials discussed during the closed session.

    5.   For a conflict of interest on a consent item, the Director shall follow steps 1 and 2 and shall not
         participate in the discussion or vote on the item but may remain in the room. If the item is
         removed from the consent agenda for separate discussion, the Director shall leave the room
         during discussion of the item.

    6.   If a Director has a personal interest in a matter on which they are disqualified, after steps 1 and
         2, the Director may leave the dais, speak from where the public addresses the Board and listen
         to the discussion of the item, but may not participate in the Board's discussion or vote.



Conflict of Interest Forms
Annual disclosure statements, known as the Statement of Economic Interests (Form 700) are required
for all Board members, designated staff, and consultants by the FPPC (Government Code Section 81000
et seq.) . These filings disclose potential conflicts of interest including sources of income, ownership of
property, and receipt of loans and gifts (see Gifts and Contributions). Additionally, CCWD's Conflict of
Interest Code, Chapter 3.08 of the CCWD Code of Regulations, identifies Board members and designated
staff as 87200 officials (Government Code Section 87200) due to their authority to manage public
investments.

Effective January L 2026, pursuant to California Senate Bill 852, 87200 officials must file their Form 700
electronically directly with the FPPC, rather than with CCWD. The District Secretary will provide Board
members with the necessary filing instructions and electronic filing links no later than February of each
year. Board members are also required to file a Form 700 when they assume office for the first time, as


                                                      Page 26

                              CCWD Board of Directors Procedures Manual - March ~2026

                                 Chapter 7: Board of Directors Meetings


well as upon leaving office. The FPPC may impose monetary penalties for late filings or for a failure to
file.


Liability
 Violations of certain laws and regulations by individual members of the Board may result in that
 member being personally liable for damages which would not be covered by CCWD's insurance.
•Examples may include discrimination, harassment, or fraud.



Gifts and Contributions
The FPPC has specific guidelines for local elected officers regarding the acceptance of gifts. Board
members may not accept gifts from any single source totaling more than $59G-630 in calendar year
January 1, 20223 - December 31, 202§4 (Section 89503) and must report single source gifts totaling
more than $50 in a calendar year.




                                                    Page 27

                            CCWD Board of Directors Procedures Manual - March ~2026
